Rationale.RP1_ImplementationReconstructability: The experiment was fully reconstructable from plan.md and demo.ipynb. The plan clearly described the hypothesis (filter heads encode portable predicates), methodology (query state patching), and expected metrics (Δ logit). The demo provided working code for all key steps. No major guesswork was required beyond adapting filter head identification for a smaller model.
Rationale.RP2_EnvironmentReproducibility: The environment was reproducible with the provided conda_env.yml and env_demo.yml template. All dependencies (transformers, torch, nnsight, baukit, circuitsvis) were installable. Model weights were available in shared_models directory. Data files were present in data_save/. Minor issues: baukit required separate pip install, env.yml needed manual path configuration.
Rationale.RP3_DeterminismAndStability: Results were stable and deterministic. Random seeds can be set for reproducibility. Model produces deterministic outputs with greedy decoding. Filter head identification and query state patching produced consistent results across multiple test cases (fruit→vehicle: Δ=+12.875, animal→furniture: Δ=+9.063). The direction and magnitude of effects matched expectations.
Rationale.RP4_DemoPresentation: The demo.ipynb is executable and demonstrates all key experiments. It shows filter head attention patterns, counterfactual sample creation, single-head and multi-head patching, and quantitative improvement in logits. All claims from plan.md are demonstrated. The demo can be run without external materials after environment setup.
